title: A Flash-Based Relativistic Collapse Model for Quantum Fields
abstract: Spontaneous collapse models provide a possible, testable solution to the quantum measurement problem, but constructing a relativistic version applicable to quantum field theory remains an important open challenge. Challenges in constructing relativistic collapse models include avoiding superluminal signaling and foliation dependence, controlling energy production, and ensuring vacuum stability. Here, we present a relativistic collapse framework that addresses these problems at the cost of introducing a new space of physical states, whose complete characterization is left open. A modified, history-dependent Aharonov--Albert prescription describes instantaneous nonlocal state updates on arbitrary spacelike foliations while preserving foliation independence. To ensure vacuum stability, we modify the standard unitary evolution through a prescription that we name dynamical vacuum subtraction. The resulting dynamical map is linear and trace-preserving but not positive on the full set of standard density operators. We establish no-signaling by proving microscopic parameter independence, and identify conditions under which standard nonrelativistic collapse dynamics are recovered. Finally, we apply our framework to a free massive scalar field, obtaining finite particle-number and energy-increase rates at leading order in the long-time regime, together with further promising evidence for the consistency of the framework.
summary: This paper proposes a novel, relativistic collapse model for quantum fields to solve the measurement problem, overcoming issues like vacuum instability. It introduces 'Dynamical Vacuum Subtraction' and applies the framework to a scalar field, deriving finite rates of particle and energy increase. The results offer quantitative evidence for the consistency of this speculative quantum gravity theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental challenge of constructing a testable, relativistic spontaneous collapse model applicable to Quantum Field Theory (QFT) to resolve the quantum measurement problem.
main_result: The authors present a framework that achieves no-signaling and yields finite particle-number and energy-increase rates for a free massive scalar field in the long-time limit.
method: The methodology involves modifying standard unitary evolution with a 'Dynamical Vacuum Subtraction' prescription and employing a history-dependent Aharonov-Albert prescription for nonlocal state updates.
model_or_system: The model is a 'Flash-Based Relativistic Collapse Model' built upon the Collapse Points Quantum Mechanics (CPQM) framework, applied to quantum fields like the free massive scalar field.
key_observables: Correlation coefficients ($r_N, r_E$), leading-order flash intensity ($\mu^{(1)}_F$), and particle/energy increase rates ($\Gamma_F$).
important_parameters: The collapse point density ($\mu_C$), the long-time limit, and the coupling constant ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the Poisson sprinkling of collapse points is statistically Poincaré invariant, and it modifies the standard dynamics to ensure vacuum stability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate state assignment on Cauchy surfaces, showing how collapse outcomes are incorporated into the state evolution across spacetime.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first outlining the challenges of relativistic collapse models, then introducing the modified Aharonov-Albert prescription and Dynamical Vacuum Subtraction, followed by detailed calculations of correlation functions and finally applying the framework to a free scalar field.
why_interesting: This work tackles the foundational intersection of quantum gravity phenomenology and quantum foundations, providing concrete, calculable predictions for collapse dynamics in QFT.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. State assignment on Cauchy surfaces. Dots denote Collapse Points (CPs), without specifying their flash/no-flash outcomes. Starting from the state on Σ0, the state assigned to a later Cauchy surface is conditioned on the CP-qubit out- comes between the two surfaces. For example, A lies to the future of Σ1 and to the past of Σ2: its outcome is included in the state assignment on Σ2, but not on Σ1.

FIG. 2. Heuristic proper-time criterion for the late-time ap- proximation. A massive one-particle wavepacket with mean momentum k0 is localized near A on Σ0 on the spatial scales relevant to the diagram. The arrow represents its approxi- mate classical trajectory, which intersects Σ1 at B; the pro- files schematically indicate the wavepacket near the two in- tersections. The proper time along this inertial segment is |B −A|. The condition |B −A| ≫τC, with τC estimated in the particle’s mean rest frame, motivates neglecting the ini- tial matter–CP correlations and the use of ΦΣ1 Σ0.
FIG. 3. Plot of the functions ˜GT (z) and ˜GS(z). For z ≫1 they both decay as ˜GT/S(z) ∼144z−6.
